To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a new approach to detect sabotage in volunteer computing is presented and evaluated, which is based on the detection of anomalous behavior of the participants; and (2) a protocol for distributed reputation-based trust management in desktop grids is introduced, which permits the participants to maintain a trust relationship with each other, and to decide whether to accept a computation or not based on the trust relationship.

(i) a mechanism for sabotage-detection can be built upon the use of cryptographic hash functions; (ii) a distributed trust-management protocol can be implemented using the concept of a distributed hash table (DHT); (iii) both the sabotage detection and trust management mechanisms can be implemented in an efficient way, with a small impact on the performance of the desktop grid.
the proposed mechanisms for sabotage detection and distributed trust management can be used to build secure and trustable desktop grids.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of techniques to increase the reliability of the desktop grid computing paradigm.

the design and evaluation of techniques that enable desktop grid computing to be used in open environments, such as the Internet, and that allow users with data-critial applications to rely on desktop grid computing.
the design and implementation of mechanisms for desktop grids that permit the detection of malicious participants and the maintenance of trust relationships among the participants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed techniques are a significant step towards the development of a secure desktop grid.
the proposed techniques can be used to improve the security and trustworthiness of desktop grids.
sabotage-tolerance and the trust management system proposed in this paper are the key elements that will allow desktop grid computing to be widely used by users with critical data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the proposed sabotage detection mechanism and the distributed trust management protocol can be integrated in a desktop grid system to provide a high degree of security and reliability, while keeping the system simple, efficient and easy to use.

we have developed mechanisms that allow one to detect failures and sabotage in desktop grids, and also to maintain a trust-based system to distinguish the trustful from the malicious participants in the computation.

the presented sabotage detection mechanism is able to detect the presence of a malicious participant with a high probability, and that the distributed trust protocol is capable to maintain a trust relationship among participants with high probability, even in a hostile environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to design a desktop grid with the capability to detect sabotage attempts and to establish trust relationships between its users and participants.
the proposed techniques can be implemented in a way that is fully transparent to the end-user and to the applications that are executed in a desktop grid.
it is possible to build desktop grids with high levels of security, and that it is possible for users to trust the results of computations run in such systems.
